correctness.rationale: For p≥5 and r≥2, each interior p-multiple index j has s=v_p(j)≤\(r-2\). Jacobsthal yields the quotient congruent to one modulo \(p^{r+2+2s}\), while the binomial coefficient has valuation \(r-1-s\), so the cube differences have valuation at least \(4r-1-s\)≥3r+1; endpoints also match. The nonmultiple binomial term, normalized by \(p^{3r}\), is \((-1)^{k-1}/k^3\) modulo p by Lucas; there are an odd number \(p^{r-1}\) of p-blocks. Bernoulli-polynomial power sums give the alternating reciprocal-cube residue \(B_{p-3}\)/2 modulo p, with p-unit denominators. Boundary r=1 is direct. The package checker independently tests 32 pairs, Bernoulli fractions, and five block decompositions, and the infinite proof does not rely on experiments.

originality.rationale: The theorem identifies the constant first nonzero p-adic digit for all prime-power Franel differences, not the known cubic divisibility. Full material read in Straub (2014), Sun (2011), and Mao (2023), plus targeted search for equivalent and stronger statements, did not reveal the leading-coefficient law. The known Jacobsthal input and classical Wolstenholme characterization are explicitly excluded from novelty claims. Unindexed/implicit stronger p-adic coverage remains a genuine risk.
